<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Company </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;border-bottom:Solid 0.75pt;padding-bottom:1pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(in thousands of dollars, except share and per share information) </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000458_dcnt_01a81709-96df-4c13-b16c-14ca4fcc46bf" continuedAt="F_000458_dcnt_c5cc41f4-c52f-4ba2-9d35-a8bf8ea3cc43">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2015 Omnibus Incentive Plan </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our Board of Directors adopted the 2015 Omnibus Incentive Plan (&#8220;Plan&#8221;) in February 2015, which became effective on May&#160;19, 2015 following stockholder approval. The Plan initially provided to grant up to an aggregate of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001325" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcTwoThousandFifteenOmnibusIncentivePlanMember_20150519" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">4,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of our common stock plus <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001326" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcTwoThousandTwelveManagementIncentivePlanMember_20150519" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">2,615,476</ix:nonFraction> shares of our common stock that were reserved for issuance under the 2012 Management Incentive Plan (&#8220;2012 MIP&#8221;) as of May&#160;19, 2015 but were not issuable pursuant to any outstanding awards. There were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001327" name="hmhc:CommonStockAdditionalCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcTwoThousandTwelveManagementIncentivePlanMember_20150519" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">10,604,071</ix:nonFraction> additional shares underlying outstanding awards under the 2012 MIP as of May&#160;19, 2015 that could have otherwise become available again for grants under the 2012 MIP in the future (by potential forfeiture, withholding or otherwise) which will instead become reserved for issuance under the Plan in the event such shares become available for future grants. On December 13, 2019, our Board of Directors approved an amendment to the Plan to allow employees to have the share withholding increased from the minimum statutory rate to a higher rate, not to exceed the maximum statutory rate. On May 19, 2020, our shareholders approved an amended and restated Plan which increased the authorization of the number of shares available for grant under the Plan by <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001328" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfAdditionalSharesAuthorized" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcTwoThousandFifteenOmnibusIncentivePlanMember_us-gaapStatementEquityComponentsAxis_us-gaapCommonStockMember_20200519_20200519" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">3,630,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of our common stock.&#160;&#160; </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our Compensation Committee may grant awards of nonqualified stock options, incentive (qualified) stock options or cash, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock awards, restricted stock units, performance compensation awards, other stock-based awards or any combination of the foregoing. Certain employees, directors, officers, consultants or advisors who have been selected by the Compensation Committee and who enter into an award agreement with respect to an award granted to them under the Plan are eligible for awards under the 2015 Omnibus Incentive Plan. The stock option awards will be granted at a strike price equal to or greater than the fair value per share of common stock as of the date of grant. The stock related to award forfeitures and stock withheld to cover tax withholding requirements upon vesting of restricted stock units remains outstanding and may be reallocated to new recipients. The purpose of the Plan is to help us attract and retain key personnel by providing them the opportunity to acquire an equity interest in our Company. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of May&#160;19, 2015, there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001329" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcTwoThousandFifteenOmnibusIncentivePlanMember_20150519" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">6,615,476</ix:nonFraction> shares authorized and available for issuance under the Plan plus any amount that could have otherwise become available again for grants under the 2012 MIP in the future by forfeiture, withholding or otherwise. As of December&#160;31, 2020, there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001330" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcTwoThousandFifteenOmnibusIncentivePlanMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">6,996,290</ix:nonFraction> shares authorized and available for future issuance under the Plan. The vesting terms for equity awards generally range from <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001331" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001580156_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcTwoThousandFifteenOmnibusIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" continuedAt="C_5a6ac481-2782-4c59-8345-6e9efe90c66d">1</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001332" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001580156_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcTwoThousandFifteenOmnibusIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">4<ix:continuation id="C_5a6ac481-2782-4c59-8345-6e9efe90c66d"> years</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric> over equal annual installments and generally expire <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001333" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardExpirationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcTwoThousandFifteenOmnibusIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">seven years</ix:nonNumeric> after the date of grant. </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Company </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;border-bottom:Solid 0.75pt;padding-bottom:1pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(in thousands of dollars, except share and per share information) </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000458_dcnt_b8d9de8b-f777-412c-a393-9fc595fe92bd" continuedAt="F_000458_dcnt_8ba50c1e-2a95-49ae-b188-1faf63725795">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2020 and 2019, we granted market-based restricted stock units to certain members of our senior management team. The number of shares ultimately issued to the recipient is based on the total shareholder return (&#8220;TSR&#8221;) of our common stock as compared to the TSR of the common stock of a peer group comprised of each member of the Russell 2000 Small Cap Market Index over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001372">three-year</span> performance measurement period. In addition, award recipients must remain employed by us throughout the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001373">three-year</span> performance measurement period to attain the full amount of the market-based units that satisfy the market performance criteria. We determined the fair value of the 2020 and 2019 market-based restricted stock units to be approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001374" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardOptionsVestedInPeriodFairValue1" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001375" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardOptionsVestedInPeriodFairValue1" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">3.1</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. We determined the fair value based on a Monte-Carlo simulation as of the date of grant, utilizing the following assumptions: the stock price on the date of grant of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001376" name="us-gaap:SharePrice" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapAwardDateAxis_hmhcGrantDateOneMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20201231" decimals="INF">4.21</ix:nonFraction> for 2020, and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001377" name="us-gaap:SharePrice" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapAwardDateAxis_hmhcGrantDateOneMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20191231" decimals="INF">7.75</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001378" name="us-gaap:SharePrice" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapAwardDateAxis_hmhcGrantDateTwoMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20191231" decimals="INF">6.71</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001379" name="us-gaap:SharePrice" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapAwardDateAxis_hmhcGrantDateThreeMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20191231" decimals="INF">6.53</ix:nonFraction> for 2019, a three-year performance measurement period, and a risk-free rate of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001380" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsRiskFreeInterestRate" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="4" scale="-2">0.40</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001381" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsRiskFreeInterestRate" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="4" scale="-2">2.51</ix:nonFraction>% for 2020 and 2019, respectively. We recognize the expense on these awards on a straight-line basis over the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001382">three-year</span> performance measurement period. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2020, there remained approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001383" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedShareBasedAwardsOtherThanOptions" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">11.9</ix:nonFraction> million of unearned compensation expense related to unvested restricted stock units to be recognized over a weighted average term of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001384" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedPeriodForRecognition1" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1.5</ix:nonNumeric> years. The restricted stock units include a combination of time-based and performance-based vesting. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employee Stock Purchase Plan </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our Board of Directors adopted an Employee Stock Purchase Plan (&#8220;ESPP&#8221;) in February 2015, which became effective on May&#160;19, 2015 following stockholder approval. The ESPP provides for up to an aggregate of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001385" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcEmployeesStockPurchasePlanMember_20150519" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million shares of our common stock may be made available for sale under the plan to eligible employees. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001386" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardDescription" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcEmployeesStockPurchasePlanMember_20200101_20201231">At the beginning of each six-month offering period under the ESPP each participant is deemed to have been granted an option to purchase shares of our common stock equal to the amount of their payroll deductions during the period, but in any event not more than five percent of the employee&#8217;s eligible compensation, subject to certain limitations. Such options may be exercised only to the extent of accumulated payroll deductions at the end of the offering period, at a purchase price per share equal to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001387" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardPurchasePriceOfCommonStockPercent" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcEmployeesStockPurchasePlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="2" scale="-2">85</ix:nonFraction>% of the fair market value of our common stock at the beginning or end of each offering period, whichever is less.</ix:nonNumeric> On December 10, 2020, the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors determined we would not start a new offering period for the ESPP until we have an opportunity to seek shareholder approval of an amended and restated ESPP. As of December&#160;31, 2020, there were a de minimis number of shares available for future issuance under the ESPP. </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000544" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfShareBasedCompensationEmployeeStockPurchasePlanActivityTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hmhcEmployeesStockPurchasePlanMember_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">1</span><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">4</span><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-weight:normal;"></span>Fair Value Measurements </p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The accounting standard for fair value measurements, among other things, defines fair value, establishes a consistent framework for measuring fair value and expands disclosure for each major asset and liability category measured at fair value on either a recurring or nonrecurring basis. The accounting standard establishes a three-tier fair value hierarchy which prioritizes the inputs used in measuring fair value as follows: </p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.24%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.24%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;1</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Observable input such as quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities&#59;</p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.24%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.24%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;2</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Observable inputs, other than the quoted prices in active markets, that are observable either directly or indirectly&#59; and</p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.24%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.24%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;3</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Unobservable inputs in which there is little or no market data, which require the reporting entity to develop its own assumptions.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets and liabilities measured at fair value are based on one or more of three valuation techniques identified in the tables below. Where more than one technique is noted, individual assets or liabilities were valued using one or more of the noted techniques. The valuation techniques are as follows: </p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.24%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.24%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(a)</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Market approach: Prices and other relevant information generated by market transactions involving identical or comparable assets or liabilities&#59; </p></td></tr></table></div>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.24%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(b)</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Cost approach: Amount that would be currently required to replace the service capacity of an asset (current replacement cost)&#59; and </p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.24%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.24%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(c)</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Income approach: Valuation techniques to convert future amounts to a single present amount based on market expectations (including present value techniques). </p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On a recurring basis, we measure certain financial assets and liabilities at fair value, including our money market funds, foreign exchange forward contracts, and interest rate derivatives contracts. The accounting standard for fair value measurements defines fair value as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. As such, fair value is a market-based measurement that should be determined based on assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or liability. In determining fair value, we utilize valuation techniques that maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs to the extent possible as well as consider counterparty and its credit risk in its assessment of fair value. </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our money market funds are classified within Level&#160;1 of the fair value hierarchy because they are valued using quoted prices in active markets for identical instruments. In addition to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001413" name="us-gaap:AssetsFairValueDisclosure" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapFairValueByAssetClassAxis_us-gaapMoneyMarketFundsMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">262.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001414" name="us-gaap:AssetsFairValueDisclosure" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapFairValueByAssetClassAxis_us-gaapMoneyMarketFundsMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">276.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million invested in money market funds as of December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, respectively, we had $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001415" name="us-gaap:AssetsFairValueDisclosure" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapFairValueByAssetClassAxis_us-gaapBankTimeDepositsMember_us-gaapFairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis_us-gaapFairValueInputsLevel1Member_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">19.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001416" name="us-gaap:AssetsFairValueDisclosure" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapFairValueByAssetClassAxis_us-gaapBankTimeDepositsMember_us-gaapFairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis_us-gaapFairValueInputsLevel1Member_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">19.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of cash invested in bank accounts as of December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, respectively. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our foreign exchange derivatives consist of forward contracts and are classified within Level&#160;2 of the fair value hierarchy because they are valued based on observable inputs and are available for substantially the full term of our derivative instruments. We use foreign exchange forward contracts to fix the functional currency value of forecasted commitments, payments and receipts. The aggregate notional amount of the outstanding foreign exchange forward contracts was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001417" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_hmhcForeignExchangeForwardContractMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">14.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001418" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_hmhcForeignExchangeForwardContractMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">15.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, respectively. Our foreign exchange forward contracts contain netting provisions to mitigate credit risk in the event of counterparty default, including payment default and cross default. At December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, the fair value of our counterparty default exposure was less than $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001419" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFairValueOfDerivativeAssetAmountOffsetAgainstCollateral" contextRef="C_0001580156_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001420" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFairValueOfDerivativeAssetAmountOffsetAgainstCollateral" contextRef="C_0001580156_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.0</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and spread across several highly rated counterparties. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our interest rate derivatives are classified within Level&#160;2 of the fair value hierarchy because they are valued based on observable inputs and are available for substantially the full term of our derivative instruments. Our interest rate risk relates primarily to U.S. dollar borrowings, partially offset by U.S. dollar cash investments. We have historically used interest rate derivative instruments to manage our earnings and cash flow exposure to changes in interest rates by converting floating-rate debt into fixed-rate debt. There were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001421" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapInterestRateSwapMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">no</ix:nonFraction> aggregate notional amounts outstanding of the interest rate derivative instruments<span style="font-size:12pt;">&#160;</span>as of December&#160;31, 2020. We designate these derivative instruments either as fair value or cash flow hedges under the accounting guidance related to derivatives and hedging. We record changes in the value of fair value hedges in interest expense, which is generally offset by changes in the fair value of the hedged debt obligation. Interest payments made or received related to our interest rate derivative instruments are included in interest expense. We record the effective portion of any change in the fair value of derivative instruments designated as cash flow hedges as unrealized gains or losses in other comprehensive loss, net of tax, until the hedged cash flow occurs, at which point the effective portion of any gain or loss is reclassified to earnings. In the event the hedged cash flow does not occur, or it becomes no longer probable that it will occur, we reclassify the amount of any gain or loss on the related cash flow hedge to interest expense at that time. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We believe we do not have significant concentrations of credit risk arising from our interest rate derivative instruments, whether from an individual counterparty or a related group of counterparties. We manage the concentration of counterparty credit risk on our interest rate derivatives instruments by limiting acceptable counterparties to a diversified group of major financial institutions with investment grade credit ratings, limiting the amount of credit exposure to each counterparty, and actively monitoring their credit ratings and outstanding fair values on an ongoing basis. Furthermore, none of our derivative transactions contain provisions that are dependent on our credit ratings from any credit rating agency. </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">107</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Company </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;border-bottom:Solid 0.75pt;padding-bottom:1pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(in thousands of dollars, except share and per share information) </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000459_dcnt_e41d03c0-76b7-4465-a7fd-d2f80efe1334" continuedAt="F_000459_dcnt_834ab59b-3cd2-4f6b-8c80-5ac2b4ebe933">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We also employ master netting arrangements that reduce our counterparty payment settlement risk on any given maturity date to the net amount of any receipts or payments due between us and the counterparty financial institution. Thus, the maximum loss due to counterparty credit risk is limited to the unrealized gains in such contracts net of any unrealized losses should any of these counterparties fail to perform as contracted. Although these protections do not eliminate concentrations of credit risk, as a result of the above considerations, we do not consider the risk of counterparty default to be significant. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Non-Financial Assets and Liabilities </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our non-financial assets, which include goodwill, other intangible assets, property, plant, and equipment, and pre-publication costs, are not required to be measured at fair value on a recurring basis. However, if certain trigger events occur, or if an annual impairment test is required, we evaluate the non-financial assets for impairment. If an impairment did occur, the asset is required to be recorded at the estimated fair value. An impairment analysis was performed for the preparation of the first quarter report, as there were triggering events for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2020 related to the decline in our stock price <span style="color:#000000;">attributed to the market environment, which resulted in a goodwill impairment</span>. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We perform an impairment test for our other intangible assets by comparing the assets fair value to its carrying value. Fair value is estimated based on recent market transactions, where available, and projected discounted cash flows, if reasonably estimable. There was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001434" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapIndefiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis_us-gaapOtherIntangibleAssetsMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001435" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapIndefiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis_us-gaapOtherIntangibleAssetsMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001433" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapIndefiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis_us-gaapOtherIntangibleAssetsMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> impairment of other intangible assets for the years ended December&#160;31, 2020, 2019 and 2018. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Non-Marketable Investments</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December 31, 2020 and 2019, the carrying value of our non-marketable investments, which were comprised of equity interests in educational technology private partnerships, was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001436" name="us-gaap:LongTermInvestments" contextRef="C_0001580156_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">4.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001437" name="us-gaap:LongTermInvestments" contextRef="C_0001580156_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively. The amounts are included in other assets in our consolidated balance sheets. Our non-marketable investments are accounted for using the cost method and are adjusted for observable transactions as appropriate. Gains from non-marketable investments were $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001438" name="us-gaap:GainLossOnInvestments" contextRef="C_0001580156_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2020 and are included in gain on investments in our consolidated statements of operations.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are involved in ordinary and routine litigation and matters incidental to our business, including claims alleging breach of contract and seeking royalty payments. Litigation alleging infringement of copyrights and other intellectual property rights is also common in the educational publishing industry. There have been various settled, pending and threatened litigation that allege we exceeded the print run limitation or other restrictions in licenses granted to us to reproduce photographs in our textbooks. <span style="font-size:12pt;">&#160;&#160;</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">While we may incur a loss associated with certain pending or threatened litigation, we are not able to estimate such amount, if any, but we do not expect any of these matters to have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial position or cash flows. We have insurance over such amounts and with coverage and deductibles as management believes is reasonable. There can be no assurance that our liability insurance will cover all events or that the limits of coverage will be sufficient to fully cover all liabilities. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In April 2019, we were notified of an unasserted claim by the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico with regards to payments in the amount of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001447" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" contextRef="C_0001580156_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_us-gaapUnassertedClaimMember_20190401_20190430" decimals="-5" scale="6">33.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million that we received in the normal course of business during the four year period prior to the May&#160;3, 2017 bankruptcy petition of the Commonwealth public instrumentalities. Management believes, based on discussions with its legal counsel, that we have meritorious defenses against such unasserted claim.&#160;The Company will vigorously defend this matter if such claim is asserted. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In September 2019, we were notified of an unasserted claim by Riverside Assessments LLC (&#8220;Riverside&#8221;) with regard to purported breaches of the Asset Purchase Agreement between the Company and Riverside dated September 12, 2018 (&#8220;APA&#8221;) and the Transition Services Agreement between the Company and Riverside dated October 1, 2018. Management believes, based on discussions with its legal counsel, that we have meritorious defenses against such unasserted claim. With regard to the alleged breaches of the APA, the APA provides that the Company may be liable only for that portion of Riverside&#8217;s damages that exceeds $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001448" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyEstimateOfPossibleLoss" contextRef="C_0001580156_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20190930" decimals="INF" scale="6">1.4</ix:nonFraction> million, and in an amount that shall not exceed $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001449" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" contextRef="C_0001580156_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_us-gaapUnassertedClaimMember_20190901_20190930" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.4</ix:nonFraction> million, which we believe would be the maximum exposure. For damages above $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001450" name="hmhc:RequirementOfWarrantyInsuranceForDamagesLimitAmount" contextRef="C_0001580156_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20190930" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.8</ix:nonFraction> million, Riverside obtained a representation and warranty insurance policy as required by the APA. The Company will vigorously defend this matter if such claim is asserted.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">109</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Company </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;border-bottom:Solid 0.75pt;padding-bottom:1pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(in thousands of dollars, except share and per share information) </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000460_dcnt_61f323db-3945-484a-b19f-a4cf5b0bfe1b">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In January 2018, Vanderbilt University (&#8220;Vanderbilt&#8221;) filed a complaint against the Company and others in connection with a license agreement originally entered into between Vanderbilt and Scholastic Inc. in 1997 and subsequently assigned to the Company as part of our acquisition of Scholastic&#8217;s Educational Technology and Services business pursuant to the stock and asset purchase agreement dated April 23, 2015. Vanderbilt alleges entitlement to additional royalties in connection with READ 180 and other products acquired from Scholastic and alleges&#160;trademark infringement in the marketing of these products. The Company is vigorously defending this matter. The case is scheduled for trial in August 2021.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with an agreement with a development content provider, we agreed to act as guarantor to that party&#8217;s loan to finance such development. Such guarantee is expected to remain until <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001451" name="hmhc:GuaranteeExpirationYear" contextRef="C_0001580156_20200101_20201231">2022</ix:nonNumeric>. Under the guarantee, we believe the maximum future payments to approximate $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001452" name="us-gaap:GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure" contextRef="C_0001580156_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">10.1</ix:nonFraction> million. In the unlikely event that we are required to make payments on behalf of the development content provider, we would have recourse against the development content provider. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We were contingently liable for $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001453" name="hmhc:ContingentLiabilityRelatedToSuretyBond" contextRef="C_0001580156_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001454" name="hmhc:ContingentLiabilityRelatedToSuretyBond" contextRef="C_0001580156_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of performance-related surety bonds for our operating activities as of December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, respectively. An aggregate of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001455" name="us-gaap:LettersOfCreditOutstandingAmount" contextRef="C_0001580156_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">18.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million<span style="font-size:12pt;">&#160;</span>and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001456" name="us-gaap:LettersOfCreditOutstandingAmount" contextRef="C_0001580156_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">23.7</ix:nonFraction> million of letters of credit existed each year at December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, respectively, of which $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001457" name="us-gaap:PledgedFinancialInstrumentsNotSeparatelyReportedSecuritiesForLetterOfCreditFacilities" contextRef="C_0001580156_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.1</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001458" name="us-gaap:PledgedFinancialInstrumentsNotSeparatelyReportedSecuritiesForLetterOfCreditFacilities" contextRef="C_0001580156_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million backed the aforementioned performance-related surety bonds each year in 2020 and 2019, respectively. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We routinely enter into standard indemnification provisions as part of license agreements involving use of our intellectual property. These provisions typically require us to indemnify and hold harmless licensees in connection with any infringement claim by a third-party relating to the intellectual property covered by the license agreement. Although the term of these provisions and the maximum potential amounts of future payments we could be required to make is not limited, we have never incurred any costs to defend or settle claims related to these types of indemnification provisions. We therefore believe the estimated fair value of these provisions is inconsequential and have <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001459" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" contextRef="C_0001580156_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001460" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" contextRef="C_0001580156_20191231" decimals="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> liabilities recorded for them as of December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019. </p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000461" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityNoteDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001580156_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2020, we had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_hmhcSegment" id="F_001509" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" contextRef="C_0001580156_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction> reportable segments (Education and HMH Books &#38; Media). Our Education segment provides educational products, technology platforms and services to meet the diverse needs of today&#8217;s classrooms. These products and services include print and digital content in the form of textbooks, digital courseware, instructional aids, educational assessment and intervention solutions, which are aimed at improving achievement and supporting learning for students who are not keeping pace with peers, professional development and school reform services. Our HMH Books &#38; Media segment primarily develops, markets and sells consumer books in print and digital formats and licenses book rights to other publishers and electronic businesses in the United </p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;border-bottom:Solid 0.75pt;padding-bottom:1pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(in thousands of dollars, except share and per share information) </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">States and abroad. The principal distribution channels for </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">HMH Books &#38; Media</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> products are retail stores, both physical and online, and wholesalers. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We measure and evaluate our reportable segments based on net sales and segment Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations. We exclude from our segments certain corporate-related expenses, as our corporate functions do not meet the definition of a segment, as defined in the accounting guidance relating to segment reporting. In addition, certain transactions or adjustments that our Chief Operating Decision Maker considers to be non-operational, such as amounts related to goodwill and other intangible asset impairment charges, derivative instruments charges, acquisition/disposition-related activity, restructuring, severance costs,  equity compensation charges, <span style="letter-spacing:-0.15pt;">gains or losses from investments, </span>gains or losses from divestitures, amortization and depreciation expenses, as well as interest and taxes, are excluded from segment Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000551" name="us-gaap:ReconciliationOfRevenueFromSegmentsToConsolidatedTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001580156_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000551_cnt_1">Although we exclude these amounts from segment Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations, they are included in reported consolidated net loss and are included in the reconciliation below.</ix:nonNumeric> </p><ix:continuation id="F_000551_cnt_1">

Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_9A_CONTROLS_PROCEDURES">Item&#160;9A. Controls and Procedures </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) and our Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (&#8220;CFO&#8221;), evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures as of December&#160;31, 2020 pursuant to Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (as amended, the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;). Based on that evaluation, our CEO and CFO have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures as of December&#160;31, 2020 were effective to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed by us in reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and forms and the information required to be disclosed by us is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our CEO and CFO, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In designing and evaluating the disclosure controls and procedures, management recognizes that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving the desired control objectives. In addition, the design of disclosure controls and procedures must reflect the fact that there are resource constraints and that management is required to apply judgment in evaluating the benefits of possible controls and procedures relative to their costs. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management of the Company is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) or 15d-15(f) promulgated under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and includes those policies and procedures that: </p>

<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;color:#auto;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;"><span style="Background-color:#auto;text-decoration:none;"></span><span style="color:#000000;"></span><span style="font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or dispositions of the Company&#8217;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements. </span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s management assessed the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December&#160;31, 2020. In making this assessment, the Company&#8217;s management used the criteria established in <span style="font-style:italic;">Internal Control-Integrated Framework (2013)</span>&#160;issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO). </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Based on our assessment and the aforementioned criteria, management concluded that, as of December&#160;31, 2020, the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting was effective. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">116</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December&#160;31, </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2020</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> has been audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in their report which appears herein in Item&#160;8 of this Annual Report</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> on Form 10-K</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting in the quarter ended December&#160;31, 2020 that materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_9B_OR_INFORMATION">Item&#160;9B. Other Information</p>
